messages:
maria: Quick question — should we switch the prefix eviction path to a deadline-based preemption model? we saw a few 200ms tail spikes when a demote waits on slow prefetches. thinking deadline would bound stall times.
dan: Do you mean a hard deadline per demotion op, or a background reclaim deadline that triggers forced eviction?
maria: Hard per-demote deadline at the handoff boundary. if we don't get residency confirmation in X ms, we mark the prefix as preempted and let the new owner load it fresh. avoids long blocking on slow peers. :thinking:
jake: Concern: preempting could cause extra cold fetches and thundering for hot prefixes. how do we avoid repeatedly preempting the same tenant?
sri: Maybe combine deadline with a short cool-down token — if we preempt a prefix, attach a preempt-penalty token for Y seconds to delay re-preemption. tokens are cheap and stored in the slab metadata.
maria: exactly — deadline + penalty token. penalty decreases priority for subsequent preemptions, so hot prefixes back off into cooperative transfer instead of constant thrash.
dan: Implementation nit: we need a safe correctness invariant for reads-in-flight during a forced preempt. on the reader side, we must detect preempted residency and transparently retry against the new owner or go through fallback. can we reuse existing lease check path?
jake: reusing lease check is fine: reader checks `lease_epoch == holder_epoch` before local KV hit. if mismatch -> fetch redirect. but need to make redirect path bounded (don't loop). add a redirect-count header.
sri: Also watch out for GC of penalty tokens after node restarts. tokens must be persisted in prefix metadata (compact) so restarts don't reset penalties and cause immediate re-thrash.
maria: good point. we'll persist a single-byte penalty marker (0..3) and expiry epoch. not heavy.
ops-bot: deploy: prefix-evict-experiment started on 10% of runtime shards at 08:12 UTC — watch latency and cold-miss rate.
dan: For metrics, we should emit: preempt_count, preempt_retry_rate, penalty_evictions, redirect_fallbacks, average_preempt_latency.
jake: And a small canary config: deadline=50ms for small prefixes, 200ms for large ones; penalty_window=30s. iterate from there.
maria: I'll draft a short RFC with invariant bullets: 1) deadline bounds handoff stall, 2) penalty tokens prevent immediate re-preempt, 3) readers use redirect-count to avoid loops, 4) tokens persisted to survive restarts. posting in #eng-runtime later today.
sri: SGTM. if someone can prototype the slab metadata layout, I can pair on the persistence path.
maria: I'll ping you. thanks all :thumbsup:
